calls.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Avalanche’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

TOR.head: We had Toronto as slight underdogs (40%), and it went Colorado’s way.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 60% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Landeskog has two goals as the Avalanche take down the Maple Leafs
paras: Darren Raddysh scored his first goal for Toronto early in the first to open the scoring. Brock Nelson and Gabriel Landeskog scored a little over a minute apart late in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Devon Toews pushed the lead to 3-1 early in the second, but Easton Cowan pulled the Maple Leafs within one with 29 seconds left in the period. The third period was a wild one. Jack Roslovic tied it up early in the period, and Landeskog scored again 51 seconds later to put the Avalanche back ahead 4-3. Artturi Lehkonen added insurance with less than three minutes left. Martin Nečas added an empty-net goal with two and a half minutes left to make it 6-3.

The Avalanche had a bit more of the good stuff. Mackenzie Blackwood made 28 saves for the Avalanche, and Sergei Bobrovsky allowed five goals on 27 shots. The Avs moved to 11-6-2 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Maple Leafs dropped to 8-10-2, seventh in the Atlantic.
